Location was established by static reading; no HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1 desynchronization was reproduced.
Exploitability depends on a deployment that translates HTTP/2 to HTTP/1 and reuses the backend connection; the advisory describes the general risk, not a specific deployment.
Only the netty-codec-http2 module was read; the org.jboss.netty:netty and io.netty:netty aggregate ranges from OSV were not individually verified.

critical_operation.description: This region is the HTTP/2 request read path. onDataRead forwards DATA payloads to the listener without comparing the received byte count to any declared Content-Length, and onHeadersRead forwards HEADERS without normalizing or storing Content-Length. RFC 7540 section 8.1.2.6 requires that mismatch to be treated as a stream error. Without it, a front-end that translates HTTP/2 to HTTP/1 can be desynchronized from the backend, enabling request smuggling. The fix adds per-stream ContentLength tracking, verifyContentLength on DATA and end-of-headers, and HttpUtil.normalizeAndGetContentLength.

entry_point.description: Inbound HTTP/2 HEADERS frames are accepted and forwarded without parsing or recording a Content-Length header.

trace.description: DATA bytes handed to the listener with no Content-Length comparison
